subject: Post-call: capacity fit + performance gating for Veridian pilot
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: capacity fit + performance gating for Veridian pilot

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo today. Quick post-call summary and the asks we agreed on so we can size a dedicated pilot: 

Recap (what Veridian told us)
- Expected steady-state: ~650 rps API requests, across 3 product endpoints (triage, summarization, clinical search).
- P95 latency target: <= 220 ms for single-turn inference (non-streaming) and <= 350 ms for streaming responses (end-to-end first-byte p95).
- Peak concurrency: spikes to ~120 active streams, typical concurrency around 40.
- Typical prompt sizes: 80% short (<= 256 tokens), 20% long (avg 1024 tokens).
- Quality: cannot quantize below FP16 for triage path; summarization path may tolerate INT8/4-bit.

Action items agreed (next steps)
1) Redwood to propose a pilot capacity configuration (GPU type + reserved throughput) that meets a 220 ms p95 SLO for non-streaming and supports streaming with low first-byte latency.
2) Veridian to share representative payload distribution (we have the sample CSV attached) and a prioritized test set for quality gating.
3) Schedule a 5-day benchmarking window where Redwood runs our harness against Veridian's sample traffic pattern.
4) Procurement/PO timeline: Alex to confirm budget contact and purchasing window by next Tue.

Open questions / asks for our engineering prep
- Please confirm whether the clinical search endpoint can accept chunked streaming (we assumed yes for the pilot).
- Any hard restrictions on model variants (no external model-hosted providers, must run on dedicated private pool)?
- Do you require HIPAA-level audit logs in the pilot (audit retention duration)?

Attachments: call recording + csv with payload breakdown.

Proposed immediate deliverable from our side: a small table of candidate configs with cost/latency tradeoffs and a recommended pilot plan (3-day smoke + 2-day steady-state). Ben / Karthik — can you take first pass on configs and run a quick back-of-envelope mapping to rps per GPU?

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Alex Novak <alex.novak@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity fit + performance gating for Veridian pilot

On Fri, 17 May 2028 at 15:12, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed immediate deliverable from our side: a small table of candidate configs with cost/latency tradeoffs and a recommended pilot plan (3-day smoke + 2-day steady-state). Ben / Karthik — can you take first pass on configs and run a quick back-of-envelope mapping to rps per GPU?

Thanks Rachel — quick initial sizing notes (back-of-envelope) based on the traffic mix you shared:

Assumptions used for the map
- Model: medium-large LLM with 8k context, FP16 for critical paths, INT8 for tolerant summarization path.
- Average output tokens per request: 120 (non-streaming), streaming paths vary.
- Network RTT 8–15 ms (us-west region).
- Batch window kept small for latency (continuous batching w/ 8–12ms windows).

Candidate GPU configurations (notes are conservative; will validate in harness)
- H100 80GB (dense): ~220–260 rps non-streaming per GPU at p95 <= 220ms for avg prompt 256 tokens; streaming first-byte p95 ~80–120 ms depending on token emission pattern. Better KV cache handling for long context.
- A100 80GB (widely available): ~160–200 rps non-streaming p95 <= 220ms. Streaming first-byte ~120–160 ms. Good stability and cost-efficiency if you can accept slightly lower steady rps.
- Multi-A100 pool with small model shard + per-request routing (preferred if you want predictable concurrency isolation): plan for 1 GPU per 150–180 rps steady-state and reserve burst capacity for spikes.

Mapping to Veridian targets (650 rps steady)
- H100 path: 3–4 GPUs reserved (3 for steady ~720 rps headroom, 4 for burst/safety).
- A100 path: 4–5 GPUs reserved (4 steady ~640 rps with tight tuning; 5 recommended for safety).

Other levers to reduce unit count
- Prefix/KV caching for frequently repeated prefixes (search + triage templates) — could save ~20–30% tokens/sec in steady-state.
- Smart routing: place summarization on INT8-capable variants to free FP16 capacity for triage.
- Adaptive batching during low latency windows.

Benchmark plan (what we'll run during the 5-day window)
- Day 0 (setup): deploy pilot pool + observability, smoke test.
- Day 1–2 (latency SLO gating): run staged 1–1.5x steady load, measure p50/p95/p99, streaming first-byte, and token throughput.
- Day 3–4 (burst tests): run synthetic spikes up to 2.5x, measure graceful degradation and fallbacks.
- Day 5 (quality gating): run prioritized test prompts to ensure INT8/quantized outputs meet quality thresholds.

I'll produce a formatted candidate table (GPU | est rps | expected p95 non-streaming | notes) by EOD Monday. Karthik / Soojin — if you have microbench numbers to layer in (tokens/sec per GPU at different batch windows), add them inline to the doc.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@veridianhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@veridianhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity fit + performance gating for Veridian pilot

Thanks Rachel / Ben — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Clinical search: yes, we can accept chunked streaming and will provide a small sample of chunking behavior in the CSV.
- Audit logs: for pilot we just need access logs and request-level IDs; HIPAA retention (90 days) will be required for production but not for the pilot.
- Model variants: we prefer everything in dedicated/private pool (no external hosted providers).

Procurement note: Priya will follow up with our purchasing team about a 60-day trial PO. She expects to have a contact and rough approval timeline by Tue EOD.

Pilot acceptance criteria we suggest
1) p95 non-streaming <= 250 ms across endpoints for the prioritized test set (we can be flexible based on cost).
2) First-byte streaming p95 <= 400 ms for clinical search.
3) No failures above 0.5% 5xx across the test window.
4) Quantized outputs pass quality gate of >=95% acceptance on the prioritized test prompts.

Happy to run the initial harness under Redwood guidance. Please send the DocuSign pilot agreement and the initial config table. We can try to kick off the harness next Thu if schedules align.

—Alex
Alex Novak
VP Product, Veridian Health
alex.novak@veridianhealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity fit + performance gating for Veridian pilot

Thanks all — short plan from infra/test engineering: 
- I'll spin up a mirrored pilot pool in our staging infra with an H100-first config and an A100 baseline. We'll run identical workloads and capture p50/p95/p99 + first-byte times for streaming.
- Test harness: will use Veridian CSV distribution (attached) and Replayer v2 to simulate realistic inter-arrival patterns + concurrent streams.
- Observability: we'll export token-level telemetry to the shared dashboard and provide a short list of SLO checks for the pilot run.
- Timeline: setup Mon-Wed (internal); smoke Thu; run 5-day window Fri–Tue. If Veridian can confirm PO cadence by Tue we can order reserved capacity and begin procurement.

Deliverables by Wed EOD: candidate GPU table (Ben), microbench numbers per GPU (Soojin), pilot runbook + dashboard link (me).

I'll also include a small script to toggle prefix caching on/off so we can quantify savings.

Karthik
